about.para1: I'm a software engineer focused on designing and building scalable digital solutions. My experience spans full-stack development, cloud platforms, APIs, enterprise integration, databases and distributed systems.
about.para2: I combine hands-on engineering with an architectural mindset — focusing on how applications, services, data and integrations work together as a complete solution, not just how individual components are built.
about.para3: My current specialization includes SAP Business Technology Platform, enterprise integration and cloud architecture, with a growing focus on solution design and how technology connects to business processes.

selectedwork.title: Selected Work
selectedwork.subtitle: Four case studies demonstrating engineering depth across integration, cloud platforms, custom software and enterprise systems.
selectedwork.confidentiality: Client information, internal architecture details and commercial data are confidential and not disclosed.
selectedwork.flow_hint: Click a node to explore how it participates in the flow
selectedwork.flow_pos_pattern: Point-of-sale transactions are published to the message queue immediately after they occur. This decouples the POS from downstream systems — the ERP and invoicing system do not need to be available when a transaction happens.
selectedwork.flow_queue_pattern: The queue absorbs traffic peaks and guarantees at-least-once delivery. Messages are only consumed when downstream systems are ready. Failed messages are routed to a Dead Letter Queue for controlled reprocessing.
selectedwork.flow_integration_pattern: Cloud integration flows consume queue messages, apply transformation and routing logic, and coordinate delivery to the ERP and invoicing system. Retry logic with backoff handles transient failures without data loss.
selectedwork.flow_erp_pattern: SAP S/4HANA receives processed ERP transactions. Idempotency controls ensure the same transaction is never posted twice, even if the integration layer retries due to a network or timeout failure.
selectedwork.flow_invoicing_pattern: Electronic invoicing receives fiscal data and returns confirmation. Priority queue handling ensures time-sensitive fiscal transactions are processed ahead of lower-priority messages.
selectedwork.case1_context: An enterprise S/4HANA implementation required near-real-time synchronization between a point-of-sale platform, integration services and ERP business processes — while meeting mandatory electronic invoicing requirements.
selectedwork.case1_challenge: The solution had to coordinate a POS platform, an integration layer, the ERP and an electronic invoicing system — each with different SLAs, reliability characteristics and data formats — under conditions of high transaction volume and strict fiscal requirements.
selectedwork.case1_contribution_intro: Designed and implemented the integration architecture connecting these systems:
selectedwork.case1_contrib1: Designed cloud integration flows coordinating data movement across all system boundaries
selectedwork.case1_contrib2: Implemented asynchronous event-based messaging with message queues for traffic peak absorption
selectedwork.case1_contrib3: Configured priority queue handling for time-sensitive transactions
selectedwork.case1_contrib4: Applied Splitter/Aggregator patterns for high-volume event processing
selectedwork.case1_contrib5: Implemented Dead Letter Queue for failed message capture and controlled reprocessing
selectedwork.case1_contrib6: Designed retry logic with backoff to handle transient failures without data loss
selectedwork.case1_contrib7: Applied idempotency controls to prevent duplicate processing under retry scenarios
selectedwork.case1_contrib8: Integrated electronic invoicing meeting fiscal compliance requirements
selectedwork.case1_contrib9: Contributed to a centralized cloud frontend for transaction visibility and operational monitoring
selectedwork.case1_decision1_desc: Queue-based messaging decouples the POS from the ERP, absorbing traffic peaks without requiring both systems to be available simultaneously — critical given their different SLAs.
selectedwork.case1_decision2_desc: Failed messages are captured in a DLQ rather than discarded, enabling controlled inspection and reprocessing without data loss or undetected failures.
selectedwork.case1_decision3_desc: All integration endpoints are designed to be idempotent — processing the same message multiple times produces the same result, making retries safe under network or system failure scenarios.
selectedwork.case1_outcome1: Reduced manual intervention in transaction processing and error recovery
selectedwork.case1_outcome2: Improved data consistency between POS, ERP and invoicing systems
selectedwork.case1_outcome3: Centralized transaction traceability across all system boundaries
selectedwork.case1_outcome4: Improved auditability for fiscal compliance requirements
selectedwork.case1_outcome5: Stronger resilience during high-volume periods through queue-based processing
selectedwork.case1_outcome6: Improved control over failed transactions through structured DLQ management
selectedwork.case1_tech: SAP Integration Suite · Cloud Integration · SAP S/4HANA · Message Queues · Splitter/Aggregator · DLQ
selectedwork.case2_context: Enterprise platforms sometimes require custom extensions to support business-specific processes that fall outside standard ERP functionality — without modifying core system configuration or creating upgrade risk.
selectedwork.case2_challenge: Design a cloud extension that integrates with the core ERP through APIs, maintains clean separation from the standard system, and can be deployed and maintained independently on a cloud platform.
selectedwork.case2_contribution_intro: Designed and implemented a side-by-side cloud extension on SAP BTP:
selectedwork.case2_contrib1: Designed the extension following the SAP BTP side-by-side pattern, keeping custom logic outside the ERP core
selectedwork.case2_contrib2: Configured Cloud Integration flows connecting the extension to ERP business processes
selectedwork.case2_contrib3: Applied API Management for structured access control and monitoring of integration endpoints
selectedwork.case2_contrib4: Deployed on Cloud Foundry with an independent release lifecycle from the ERP
selectedwork.case2_contrib5: Implemented connectivity and security following SAP BTP platform standards
selectedwork.case2_decision1_desc: Keeping custom logic outside the ERP core eliminates upgrade risk — the extension evolves independently of ERP release cycles. This decoupling justifies the additional infrastructure overhead.
selectedwork.case2_decision2_title: API Management as the integration boundary
selectedwork.case2_decision2_desc: API Management provides a controlled, observable integration boundary between the extension and ERP — enforcing access policies and providing monitoring without coupling the systems directly.
selectedwork.case2_outcome1: A cloud extension supporting a business-specific enterprise process, integrated with the ERP through APIs
selectedwork.case2_outcome2: Clean separation from core ERP — no impact on standard system behavior or upgrade paths
selectedwork.case2_outcome3: Independently deployable and maintainable on SAP BTP / Cloud Foundry
selectedwork.case2_tech: SAP BTP · Cloud Integration · API Management · Cloud Foundry · SAP Build · SAP Build Work Zone
selectedwork.case3_context: A business required a B2B SaaS platform covering inventory management, billing and accounting — while maintaining strict data isolation between tenants on shared infrastructure.
selectedwork.case3_challenge: Design a multi-tenant architecture that guarantees data isolation at the database level, remains maintainable as business logic grows, and supports future integrations — without compromising performance or security.
selectedwork.case3_contribution_intro: Designed and built the full application architecture:
selectedwork.case3_contrib1: Designed the multi-tenant data isolation strategy using Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL
selectedwork.case3_contrib2: Structured business services by domain: POS operations, inventory, invoicing, customer management
selectedwork.case3_contrib3: Implemented a centralized Auth Service issuing HttpOnly cookies — tokens never exposed to client-side JavaScript
selectedwork.case3_contrib4: Configured SAP Application Router for centralized routing and JWT validation
selectedwork.case3_contrib5: Deployed the full distributed application on SAP BTP / Cloud Foundry using declarative MTA descriptors
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer1_desc: Responsive client application handling POS operations, inventory, invoicing, customer management and sales analytics.
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer2_tech: SAP Application Router · JWT Validation · Route Config
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer2_desc: Centralizes routing and authorization. Validates JWT tokens and forwards user context via internal headers — security concerns outside individual services.
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer3_tech: Node.js · SAP CAP · REST APIs · Auth Service
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer3_desc: Domain-separated services: POS operations, inventory, invoicing engine, customer management. Auth Service manages sessions with HttpOnly, Secure cookies.
selectedwork.case3_arch_layer4_desc: Multi-tenant database with RLS ensuring strict data isolation at the database level — structurally impossible to leak cross-tenant data, even under application bugs.
selectedwork.case3_eng_intro: Real technical challenges encountered and how they were resolved:
selectedwork.case3_eng1_decision: Use a declarative multi-target deployment model to handle service dependencies and ordering consistently across all environments.
selectedwork.case3_eng1_solution: MTA (Multi-Target Application) patterns using mta.yaml for declarative deployments on Cloud Foundry.
selectedwork.case3_eng1_outcome: Consistent, repeatable deployments across dev, staging and production with automated dependency management.
selectedwork.case3_eng2_decision: Centralize authentication in a dedicated service and propagate identity via internal headers — tokens never exposed to client-side JavaScript.
selectedwork.case3_eng2_solution: A dedicated Auth Service issues HttpOnly, Secure cookies. The Application Router validates tokens and forwards user context internally.
selectedwork.case3_eng2_outcome: Secure session management with no token exposure, even when multiple services handle a single request.
selectedwork.case3_eng3_decision: Apply security at the database level to make isolation a structural guarantee, not an application convention.
selectedwork.case3_eng3_solution: Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL combined with a tenant-aware ORM layer scoping every query automatically.
selectedwork.case3_eng3_outcome: Cross-tenant data access structurally impossible at the database level, regardless of application behavior.
selectedwork.case3_outcome1: A functional B2B SaaS platform integrating inventory, billing and accounting
selectedwork.case3_outcome2: Strong multi-tenant isolation guaranteed at the database level — not dependent on application correctness
selectedwork.case3_outcome3: Distributed architecture with clear layer separation, deployed on SAP BTP
selectedwork.case3_tech: Next.js · Node.js · SAP CAP · PostgreSQL · RLS · SAP BTP · Cloud Foundry · MTA
selectedwork.case4_context: Maintenance teams lacked centralized visibility into equipment, work orders, tasks, priorities, deadlines and maintenance schedules — leading to coordination gaps and reactive rather than planned maintenance.
selectedwork.case4_challenge: Model operational workflows with enough structure for traceability, prioritization and scheduling, while keeping the system maintainable and extensible as operational requirements evolve.
selectedwork.case4_contribution_intro: Designed and built the system covering the full maintenance workflow lifecycle:
selectedwork.case4_contrib1: Modeled work order lifecycle as explicit state machines, enforcing only valid transitions between states
selectedwork.case4_contrib2: Built task priority and deadline tracking into the data model — not derived at query time
selectedwork.case4_contrib3: Implemented alert logic triggered by threshold conditions, not manual review
selectedwork.case4_contrib4: Designed equipment and work order relationships for maintainability and future extensibility
selectedwork.case4_decision1_desc: Work orders follow a defined state machine rather than free-form status fields. This prevents invalid transitions, simplifies business logic and makes workflow behavior auditable.
selectedwork.case4_decision2_desc: Priority and deadline data lives in the model, not computed on read. This simplifies querying, sorting and alerting without runtime complexity.
selectedwork.case4_outcome1: Centralized operational system with full visibility into equipment and maintenance workflows
selectedwork.case4_outcome2: Structured maintenance workflows with traceability and prioritization built in
selectedwork.case4_outcome3: Reduced reliance on manual coordination for scheduling and task tracking
selectedwork.case4_tech: React · Node.js · PostgreSQL · REST APIs · Workflow State Management
